content: 1. The World Health Organization (WHO) provides recommendations for the use of hormonal contraception in women living with HIV who are undergoing antiretroviral therapy (ART). These recommendations are part of updated guidelines on first-line and second-line antiretroviral regimens, post-exposure prophylaxis, and early infant diagnosis of HIV. 2. Women taking nucleoside/nucleotide reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NRTIs) can use all hormonal contraceptive methods without restriction. This includes combined oral contraceptives (COCs), combined injectable contraceptives (CICs), contraceptive patches, vaginal rings, progestogen-only pills (POPs), progestogen-only injectables (POIs) such as depot medroxyprogesterone acetate (DMPA) and norethisterone enanthate (NET-EN), and implants containing levonorgestrel (LNG) or etonogestrel (ETG). These are classified as Medical Eligibility Criteria (MEC) Category 1. 3. Women taking NRTIs can generally use the levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine device (LNG-IUD) (MEC Category 2), provided their HIV clinical disease is asymptomatic or mild (WHO Stage 1 or 2). However, women with severe or advanced HIV clinical disease (WHO Stage 3 or 4) should generally not initiate LNG-IUD use (MEC Category 3 for initiation) until their condition improves to asymptomatic or mild disease. 4. Women taking NRTIs who already have an LNG-IUD inserted and later develop severe or advanced HIV clinical disease do not need to have the IUD removed. This is classified as MEC Category 2 for continuation. 5. Women using non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NNRTIs) containing efavirenz or nevirapine can generally use COCs, CICs, contraceptive patches, vaginal rings, POPs, NET-EN, and LNG or ETG implants (MEC Category 2). They can use DMPA without restriction (MEC Category 1). 6. Women taking NNRTIs can generally use the LNG-IUD (MEC Category 2) if their HIV clinical disease is asymptomatic or mild (WHO Stage 1 or 2). However, those with severe or advanced HIV clinical disease (WHO Stage 3 or 4) should not initiate LNG-IUD use (MEC Category 3 for initiation) until their condition improves to asymptomatic or mild disease. 7. Women taking NNRTIs who already have an LNG-IUD inserted and later develop severe or advanced HIV clinical disease do not need to have the IUD removed (MEC Category 2 for continuation). 8. Women using protease inhibitors (PIs), including those boosted with ritonavir, can generally use COCs, CICs, contraceptive patches, vaginal rings, POPs, NET-EN, and LNG or ETG implants (MEC Category 2). They can use DMPA without restriction (MEC Category 1). 9. Women taking PIs can generally use the LNG-IUD (MEC Category 2) if their HIV clinical disease is asymptomatic or mild (WHO Stage 1 or 2). However, those with severe or advanced HIV clinical disease (WHO Stage 3 or 4) should not initiate LNG-IUD use (MEC Category 3 for initiation) until their condition improves to asymptomatic or mild disease. 10. Women taking PIs who already have an LNG-IUD inserted and later develop severe or advanced HIV clinical disease do not need to have the IUD removed (MEC Category 2 for continuation). 11. Women using the integrase inhibitor raltegravir can use all hormonal contraceptive methods without restriction (MEC Category 1). This includes COCs, CICs, contraceptive patches, vaginal rings, POPs, POIs, and implants containing LNG or ETG. 12. Women taking raltegravir can generally use the LNG-IUD (MEC Category 2) if their HIV clinical disease is asymptomatic or mild (WHO Stage 1 or 2). However, those with severe or advanced HIV clinical disease (WHO Stage 3 or 4) should not initiate LNG-IUD use (MEC Category 3 for initiation) until their condition improves to asymptomatic or mild disease. 13. Women taking raltegravir who already have an LNG-IUD inserted and later develop severe or advanced HIV clinical disease do not need to have the IUD removed (MEC Category 2 for continuation). 14. The MEC categories for contraceptive eligibility are as follows: Category 1: No restriction for the use of the contraceptive method. Category 2: The advantages of using the method generally outweigh the theoretical or proven risks. Category 3: The theoretical or proven risks usually outweigh the advantages of using the method. Category 4: The method represents an unacceptable health risk if used. 15. These recommendations are based on the WHO’s Medical Eligibility Criteria for Contraceptive Use, 5th edition, published in 2015.
